elements.evidence: The rendered clause still binds Customer: "neither party will solicit any person employed by the other party who is or was directly involved in such services to leave his or her employment with that party." A mutual covenant still imposes a restriction on Licensee (Customer), so the preferred no-non-solicit outcome is not achieved. The drafter would need to delete Article X(b) in its entirety to reach the preferred level.

Rewritten first sentence reads "neither party will solicit any person employed by the other party ... to leave his or her employment with that party", replacing the one-sided "the Licensee will not solicit any person employed by Licensor and/or its Affiliates".

elements.element: The restriction covers only personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: Scope is limited to "any person employed by the other party who is or was directly involved in such services", i.e. "the services provided under this Agreement", replacing the prior reach over every person employed by Licensor and its Affiliates.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months after the person's involvement ends.
elements.evidence: "During the period of twelve (12) months after the end of that person's involvement in the services provided under this Agreement"; the standing "During the Term of this Agreement and during the three year period after the expiration or termination" limb is deleted, so no residual limb can extend the covenant.

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Retained verbatim in the definition of "Solicit": "shall not mean generally advertising job openings or any activities that constitute follow-up to individuals who respond to job opening advertisements".

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Retained verbatim: "or who voluntarily initiate employment inquiries" within the "Solicit" definition, which excludes persons approaching of their own accord.

elements.element: The restriction does not prohibit hiring.
elements.evidence: The operative prohibition is only on soliciting a person "to leave his or her employment"; "Solicit" is defined as "affirmative recruitment specifically aimed at one or more individuals identified by name, title or affiliation". No "employ or engage" or no-hire language appears anywhere in the rendered clause.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete on the operative language: mutuality, involvement-based scope, a single 12-month post-involvement cap, and the two pre-existing carve-outs, with no hire prohibition.

Preferred level is not met because a restriction (albeit mutual) still binds Customer; only deletion of Article X(b) would satisfy it. Deviation status is correct because the original ran for the Term plus three years over all Licensor and Affiliate personnel, which is past the 24-month/all-personnel walk-away line.

Minimality holds: only the first sentence was rewritten, and each change (party direction, personnel scope, duration) maps to a selected fallback element; the definition of "Solicit" carrying the carve-outs is retained verbatim with no added survival tails, procedures, or extra obligations. Dropping "and/or its Affiliates" is absorbed by the mutual "other party"/directly-involved scope rewrite rather than an unrelated deletion.

Intent is preserved: no defined term is orphaned ("Solicit" is still defined in the same paragraph, and "services provided under this Agreement" is used descriptively, not as an undefined capitalised term), no cross-reference dangles, and no retained sentence contradicts the new period.
Drafting note for the record, not a defect: the covenant now bites only in the 12-month window after involvement ends, which is at or better than the fallback anchor and favourable to Customer.
